name: _incompatible_extension_module_restrictions
doc:
A context manager that can temporarily skip the compatibility check.

NOTE: This function is meant to accommodate an unusual case; one
which is likely to eventually go away.  There's is a pretty good
chance this is not what you were looking for.

WARNING: Using this function to disable the check can lead to
unexpected behavior and even crashes.  It should only be used during
extension module development.

If "disable_check" is True then the compatibility check will not
happen while the context manager is active.  Otherwise the check
*will* happen.

Normally, extensions that do not support multiple interpreters
may not be imported in a subinterpreter.  That implies modules
that do not implement multi-phase init or that explicitly of out.

Likewise for modules import in a subinterpreter with its own GIL
when the extension does not support a per-interpreter GIL.  This
implies the module does not have a Py_mod_multiple_interpreters slot
set to Py_MOD_PER_INTERPRETER_GIL_SUPPORTED.

In both cases, this context manager may be used to temporarily
disable the check for compatible extension modules.

You can get the same effect as this function by implementing the
basic interface of multi-phase init (PEP 489) and lying about
support for multiple interpreters (or per-interpreter GIL).

name: cache_from_source
doc:
Given the path to a .py file, return the path to its .pyc file.

The .py file does not need to exist; this simply returns the path to the
.pyc file calculated as if the .py file were imported.

The 'optimization' parameter controls the presumed optimization level of
the bytecode file. If 'optimization' is not None, the string representation
of the argument is taken and verified to be alphanumeric (else ValueError
is raised).

If sys.implementation.cache_tag is None then NotImplementedError is raised.

changed.text: The optimization parameter was added and the debug_override parameter was deprecated.

name: decode_source
doc:
Decode bytes representing source code and return the string.

Universal newline support is used in the decoding.

name: find_spec
doc:
Return the spec for the specified module.

First, sys.modules is checked to see if the module was already imported. If
so, then sys.modules[name].__spec__ is returned. If that happens to be
set to None, then ValueError is raised. If the module is not in
sys.modules, then sys.meta_path is searched for a suitable spec with the
value of 'path' given to the finders. None is returned if no spec could
be found.

If the name is for submodule (contains a dot), the parent module is
automatically imported.

The name and package arguments work the same as importlib.import_module().
In other words, relative module names (with leading dots) work.

changed.text: Raises ModuleNotFoundError instead of AttributeError if package is in fact not a package (i.e. lacks a __path__ attribute).

name: LazyLoader
doc: A loader that creates a module which defers loading until attribute access.

changed.text: Began calling create_module(), removing the compatibility warning for importlib.machinery.BuiltinImporter and importlib.machinery.ExtensionFileLoader.

name: factory
doc: Construct a callable which returns the eager loader made lazy.

name: MAGIC_NUMBER
doc: The bytes which represent the bytecode version number. If you need help with loading/writing bytecode then consider importlib.abc.SourceLoader.

name: module_from_spec
doc: Create a module based on the provided spec.

name: resolve_name
doc: Resolve a relative module name to an absolute one.

changed.text: To improve consistency with import statements, raise ImportError instead of ValueError for invalid relative import attempts.

name: source_from_cache
doc:
Given the path to a .pyc. file, return the path to its .py file.

The .pyc file does not need to exist; this simply returns the path to
the .py file calculated to correspond to the .pyc file.  If path does
not conform to PEP 3147/488 format, ValueError will be raised. If
sys.implementation.cache_tag is None then NotImplementedError is raised.

name: source_hash
doc: Return the hash of *source_bytes* as used in hash-based pyc files.

name: spec_from_file_location
doc:
Return a module spec based on a file location.

To indicate that the module is a package, set
submodule_search_locations to a list of directory paths.  An
empty list is sufficient, though its not otherwise useful to the
import system.

The loader must take a spec as its only __init__() arg.

name: spec_from_loader
doc: Return a module spec based on various loader methods.
